subject.title: [Bug]: Feishu streaming card full-content updates cause severe latency regression on long replies

question: Should the Feishu plugin support an explicit opt-in append/delta streaming-card mode for deployments where CardKit full-content updates create multi-minute long-reply latency, or should OpenClaw preserve full-content-only behavior and pursue another fix?
rationale: The source-backed regression is real enough to keep open, but adding an append/content mode changes Feishu plugin behavior and config surface despite official docs favoring full-content updates.

options.title: Sponsor opt-in append mode
options.body: Keep full-content as the default, add a documented per-account opt-in append or transport mode with warning text, regression tests, and redacted live Feishu proof.

options.title: Require full-content mitigation only
options.body: Reject append mode for now and require https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/91943 or a replacement to prove improved latency while still sending full-content payloads.

options.title: Document workaround only
options.body: Leave runtime behavior unchanged and document disabling streaming cards for affected deployments until stronger Feishu API evidence appears.

recommendation.title: Sponsor opt-in append mode
recommendation.body: Keep full-content as the default, add a documented per-account opt-in append or transport mode with warning text, regression tests, and redacted live Feishu proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The package metadata points to m1heng as the Feishu plugin community owner, and the decision is specific to Feishu channel behavior.
